newsitem.title: USA: Group questions utility deregulation claims.
newsitem.headline: Group questions utility deregulation claims.

text.p: The Electric Consumers' Alliance said Tuesday Congressional proposals to deregulate the nation's electric utilities are based on questionable claims.
The consumer group, which represents more than 150 organizations, said highly touted claims of huge savings under competition are best likened to cold fusion.
The alliance said many of the dramatic conclusions of a study being used by lawmakers to support federal deregulation legislation are based on "fundamental and serious" errors.
Alliance executive director Robert Johnson said the group was referring to a study by Citizens for Sound Economy.
He said the 43 percent decline in electricity rates it predicts is based on a series of misleading premises.

"To the extent this study serves as a basis for legislation ... it should not be relied on," he told a news conference introducing an analysis the alliance did of the assumptions in the Citizens for Sound Economy study.
